item.title: Stand Firm
item.description:
One of the hardest parts of being a father is standing firm when the world is constantly trying to pull you away.

Every day there is another voice telling our children what they should believe, who they should become, and what they should value. But truth doesn't become less true just because the world changes its mind.

As fathers, we have to become the pillar our children can lean on when everything around them feels uncertain.

item.title: The Trail Always Teaches
item.description:
Some lessons can't be taught. They have to be lived.

Every summer, my daughters and I pack up the car and head somewhere new.

Some people think it's about the destination. The mountains. The lakes. The cabins.

Those things are great, but they're not the reason we go. The real reason is the trail.

Before we start, I tell my girls the same thing every time: "This is life."

Read the full post at obsidianmusic.org/blog.html

item.title: Presence Over Perfection
item.description:
Fatherhood isn't about getting everything right. It's about refusing to stop showing up.

I still remember the moment my wife told me we were going to have a baby. For a second, everything stood still.

I wish I could tell you my first emotion was excitement—that I immediately pictured teaching my child to ride a bike or cheering from the stands at every game and recital.

It wasn't. It was fear.

Not because I didn't want to be a father, but because I had no idea what being a father actually looked like.
